argv:
Rewrite the text following the Microsoft writing style.

Sound like a helpful colleague chatting with the reader, not a manual. Use
contractions everywhere they'd naturally occur, address the reader directly as
"you", and reach for everyday words over formal ones. A sentence fragment is
fine when it lands the point — don't force every thought into a full clause.

Open with the single thing the reader most needs to know, then explain. Keep
sentences short and let the page's shape (headings, short paragraphs) do some
of the work.

Use sentence case for any heading. Use the active voice and the present tense.
Tell the reader exactly what to do and what happens next, in a tone that feels
like a quick conversation rather than a document.

Skip jargon, hedging, and anything that talks down to the reader — but don't
skip the personality. A little warmth and a casual aside are welcome.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text:
Lower the guard to the recommended clearance above the workpiece before you engage the blade. Check the tensioning wheel a few times each shift, too — tension can drift even if the machine's been sitting idle.

Changed the blade? Check the lower blade guide for wear. If the new blade matches the old one's width and pitch, a quick visual check is fine — just make sure you've run through the tensioning procedure first (see elsewhere in this manual).

Skip the loose clothing and jewelry around this machine, and tie back long hair.

Wait until the blade's come to a complete stop before you step away. And give it a few minutes after that — the machine stays hot longer than you'd think, so be careful.
